quiz.question: [Setup] Import NumPy using the conventional alias np:________
quiz.explanation: This imports the NumPy package and binds it to the conventional short name np, which is used throughout most NumPy code.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a NumPy array from the Python list [1, 2, 3]:________
quiz.explanation: np.array() converts a Python sequence into a NumPy ndarray. NumPy arrays support vectorized operations and multidimensional indexing.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a 2×3 array filled with zeros:________
quiz.explanation: np.zeros() creates an array of the requested shape with every element initialized to 0.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a 2×3 array filled with ones:________
quiz.explanation: np.ones() creates an array of the requested shape with every element initialized to 1.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a 2×3 array filled with the value 7:________
quiz.explanation: np.full() creates an array of the requested shape and fills every element with the supplied value.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Allocate a 2×3 array without initializing its values:________
quiz.explanation: np.empty() allocates an array without setting its entries to a known value. Its initial contents are whatever data already exists in that memory.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create an array containing 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8:________
quiz.explanation: np.arange(start, stop, step) works similarly to Python range(), but returns a NumPy array. The stop value is excluded.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create 5 evenly spaced values from 0 through 1 inclusive:________
quiz.explanation: np.linspace(start, stop, num) creates a fixed number of evenly spaced values and includes the endpoint by default.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a 3×3 identity matrix:________
quiz.explanation: np.eye(3) creates a square matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

quiz.question: [Array Creation] Create a 2×3 array of random floating-point values in [0, 1) using the older random API:________
quiz.explanation: np.random.rand() creates random floating-point values uniformly distributed over [0, 1). For new code, NumPy generally recommends default_rng().

quiz.question: [Array Properties] Get the shape of array a:________
quiz.explanation: The shape attribute returns a tuple containing the length of each dimension of the array.

quiz.question: [Array Properties] Get the number of dimensions of array a:________
quiz.explanation: The ndim attribute returns how many axes or dimensions the array has.

quiz.question: [Array Properties] Get the total number of elements in array a:________
quiz.explanation: The size attribute returns the total element count across all dimensions.

quiz.question: [Array Properties] Get the element data type of array a:________
quiz.explanation: The dtype attribute describes the NumPy data type used to store the elements.

quiz.question: [Array Properties] Get the number of bytes used by each element of array a:________
quiz.explanation: The itemsize attribute returns the size in bytes of one array element.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get the first element of one-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: NumPy uses zero-based indexing, so index 0 accesses the first element.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get the last element of one-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: A negative index counts from the end, so -1 accesses the last element.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get elements at indices 1 through 3 from array a:________
quiz.explanation: Slice notation includes the start index and excludes the stop index.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get every other element from array a starting at index 0:________
quiz.explanation: The third slice component is the step. A step of 2 selects every second element.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get the element at row 0, column 1 of a two-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: For a 2D NumPy array, a[row, column] directly indexes the requested cell.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get the first row of a two-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: The colon selects all columns, so a[0, :] returns row 0.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get the second column of a two-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: The colon selects all rows, while column index 1 selects the second column.

quiz.question: [Indexing & Slicing] Get columns 1 and 2 from every row of a two-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: This selects every row and columns from index 1 up to but not including index 3.

quiz.question: [Boolean Filtering] Select only elements of array a that are greater than 10:________
quiz.explanation: The expression a > 10 creates a Boolean mask, and indexing with that mask returns only elements where the mask is True.

quiz.question: [Boolean Filtering] Select elements of array a that are greater than 5 and less than 20:________
quiz.explanation: NumPy combines element-wise Boolean conditions with &, and each comparison should be wrapped in parentheses.

quiz.question: [Boolean Filtering] Select elements of array a satisfying either condition cond1 or condition cond2:________
quiz.explanation: The | operator performs element-wise logical OR on Boolean arrays or masks.

quiz.question: [Boolean Filtering] Select elements of array a for which Boolean mask is False:________
quiz.explanation: The ~ operator negates a Boolean array element by element, turning True into False and False into True.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Reshape array a into 2 rows and 3 columns:________
quiz.explanation: reshape() changes the array's dimensional layout without changing the total number of elements.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Return a flattened one-dimensional copy of array a:________
quiz.explanation: flatten() returns a new one-dimensional copy of the array, so modifying it does not modify the original array.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Return a flattened one-dimensional view of array a when possible:________
quiz.explanation: ravel() returns a flattened array and uses a view when possible, which can avoid an unnecessary copy.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Transpose array a using its shorthand attribute:________
quiz.explanation: The .T attribute returns the transpose, swapping axes for a 2D matrix so rows become columns and vice versa.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Transpose array a using a NumPy function:________
quiz.explanation: np.transpose() permutes an array's axes. With a 2D array and no explicit axes, it swaps rows and columns.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Remove dimensions of length 1 from array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.squeeze() removes axes whose size is 1 while leaving other dimensions unchanged.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Add a new axis at position 0 to array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.expand_dims() inserts a new dimension of size 1 at the specified axis.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Reshape one-dimensional array a into a column vector:________
quiz.explanation: Using -1 tells NumPy to infer that dimension automatically. The result has one column and as many rows as needed.

quiz.question: [Reshaping] Reshape one-dimensional array a into a row vector:________
quiz.explanation: Using -1 tells NumPy to infer the number of columns automatically, producing a single-row 2D array.

quiz.question: [Combining Arrays] Join arrays a and b along an existing axis:________
quiz.explanation: np.concatenate() joins arrays along an existing axis and does not create a new stacking dimension.

quiz.question: [Combining Arrays] Stack arrays a and b along a new axis:________
quiz.explanation: np.stack() joins arrays by creating a new axis, so the output has one more dimension than the inputs.

quiz.question: [Combining Arrays] Stack arrays a and b vertically:________
quiz.explanation: np.vstack() stacks arrays row-wise, which is convenient for building a taller 2D array.

quiz.question: [Combining Arrays] Stack arrays a and b horizontally:________
quiz.explanation: np.hstack() joins arrays horizontally; for one-dimensional inputs, it concatenates them into a longer 1D array.

quiz.question: [Splitting Arrays] Split array a into 4 equal parts:________
quiz.explanation: np.split() divides an array into the requested number of equal pieces and raises an error if an equal split is impossible.

quiz.question: [Splitting Arrays] Split array a into 3 parts even when equal-sized parts are impossible:________
quiz.explanation: np.array_split() allows uneven pieces, unlike np.split(), which requires equal division.

quiz.question: [Splitting Arrays] Split a two-dimensional array a vertically into separate row groups:________
quiz.explanation: np.vsplit() splits an array along its first axis, which corresponds to separating row groups in a 2D array.

quiz.question: [Splitting Arrays] Split a two-dimensional array a horizontally into separate column groups:________
quiz.explanation: np.hsplit() splits an array along its second axis, which corresponds to separating column groups in a 2D array.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Add arrays a and b element by element:________
quiz.explanation: NumPy's + operator performs element-wise addition when the array shapes are compatible.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Subtract array b from array a element by element:________
quiz.explanation: NumPy's - operator performs element-wise subtraction.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Multiply arrays a and b element by element:________
quiz.explanation: The * operator performs element-wise multiplication, not matrix multiplication.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Divide array a by array b element by element:________
quiz.explanation: The / operator performs element-wise division and normally produces floating-point results.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Square every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: The ** operator applies exponentiation element by element, so each value in a is squared.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Add arrays a and b using NumPy's explicit function:________
quiz.explanation: np.add() is the function form of element-wise addition and is equivalent to a + b.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Subtract array b from array a using NumPy's explicit function:________
quiz.explanation: np.subtract() performs element-wise subtraction and is equivalent to a - b.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Multiply arrays a and b using NumPy's explicit function:________
quiz.explanation: np.multiply() performs element-wise multiplication and is equivalent to a * b.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Divide array a by array b using NumPy's explicit function:________
quiz.explanation: np.divide() performs element-wise division and is equivalent to a / b.

quiz.question: [Element-wise Arithmetic] Raise every element of array a to the second power using a NumPy function:________
quiz.explanation: np.power() performs element-wise exponentiation.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the square root of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.sqrt() computes element-wise square roots.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute e raised to each element of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.exp() computes the exponential e**x for every element.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the natural logarithm of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.log() computes the natural logarithm element by element.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the base-10 logarithm of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.log10() computes the base-10 logarithm element by element.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the absolute value of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.abs() returns the element-wise absolute value.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the sine of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.sin() computes the element-wise sine, with inputs interpreted in radians.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the cosine of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.cos() computes the element-wise cosine, with inputs interpreted in radians.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Compute the tangent of every element in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.tan() computes the element-wise tangent, with inputs interpreted in radians.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Round every element in array a downward to the nearest integer:________
quiz.explanation: np.floor() returns the greatest integer value less than or equal to each element.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Round every element in array a upward to the nearest integer:________
quiz.explanation: np.ceil() returns the smallest integer value greater than or equal to each element.

quiz.question: [Mathematical Functions] Round every element in array a to the nearest value using NumPy's rounding function:________
quiz.explanation: np.round() rounds array values element by element.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the sum of all elements in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.sum() adds all elements when no axis is specified.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the arithmetic mean of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.mean() returns the average of the array values.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the median of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.median() returns the middle value, or the average of the two middle values for an even number of items.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Get the minimum value in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.min() returns the smallest value in the array.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Get the maximum value in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.max() returns the largest value in the array.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the standard deviation of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.std() computes the standard deviation of the array values.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the variance of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.var() computes the variance of the array values.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the product of all elements in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.prod() multiplies all array elements together.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the cumulative sum of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.cumsum() returns running totals across the flattened array by default.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the cumulative product of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.cumprod() returns running products across the flattened array by default.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the sum of array a down the rows, producing one result per column:________
quiz.explanation: axis=0 reduces the first dimension, so for a 2D array the result contains one sum per column.

quiz.question: [Aggregation & Statistics] Compute the sum of array a across the columns, producing one result per row:________
quiz.explanation: axis=1 reduces the second dimension, so for a 2D array the result contains one sum per row.

quiz.question: [Min/Max Locations] Get the index of the smallest element in one-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.argmin() returns the index of the minimum value. Without an axis, multidimensional arrays are treated as flattened.

quiz.question: [Min/Max Locations] Get the index of the largest element in one-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.argmax() returns the index of the maximum value. Without an axis, multidimensional arrays are treated as flattened.

quiz.question: [Searching] Find the indices where array a is equal to 30:________
quiz.explanation: With only a condition, np.where() returns a tuple of index arrays indicating where the condition is True.

quiz.question: [Searching] Get the one-dimensional indices where array a is greater than 20:________
quiz.explanation: For a 1D array, np.where(condition) returns a one-item tuple; indexing [0] extracts the array of matching indices.

quiz.question: [Searching] Create an array containing 1 where a is greater than 20 and 0 otherwise:________
quiz.explanation: With three arguments, np.where(condition, x, y) chooses x where the condition is True and y where it is False.

quiz.question: [Searching] Get the indices of all nonzero elements in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.nonzero() returns a tuple of index arrays identifying every nonzero element.

quiz.question: [Condition Checks] Check whether at least one element of array a is greater than 2:________
quiz.explanation: np.any() returns True if at least one element of the Boolean array is True.

quiz.question: [Condition Checks] Check whether every element of array a is greater than 0:________
quiz.explanation: np.all() returns True only if every element of the Boolean array is True.

quiz.question: [Sorting] Return a sorted copy of array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.sort() returns a sorted array rather than modifying a in place by default.

quiz.question: [Sorting] Return the indices that would sort array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.argsort() returns index positions in the order that would arrange the array from smallest to largest.

quiz.question: [Unique Values] Return the sorted unique values in array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.unique() removes duplicate values and returns the distinct values, sorted by default.

quiz.question: [Unique Values] Get each unique value in array a together with how many times it occurs:________
quiz.explanation: Setting return_counts=True returns both the unique values and a parallel array containing their occurrence counts.

quiz.question: [Set Operations] Get values that appear in both one-dimensional arrays a and b:________
quiz.explanation: np.intersect1d() returns the sorted intersection of two one-dimensional arrays.

quiz.question: [Set Operations] Get the sorted union of one-dimensional arrays a and b:________
quiz.explanation: np.union1d() returns the unique values appearing in either array.

quiz.question: [Set Operations] Get values that appear in array a but not in array b:________
quiz.explanation: np.setdiff1d() returns the unique values in a that are not present in b.

quiz.question: [Set Operations] Check element by element whether values of array a appear in array b:________
quiz.explanation: np.isin() returns a Boolean array with the same shape as a, indicating whether each element occurs in b.

quiz.question: [Set Operations] Select from array a only the values that are either 2 or 3:________
quiz.explanation: np.isin() creates the membership mask, and Boolean indexing uses that mask to filter a.

quiz.question: [Copying] Create an independent copy of NumPy array a and assign it to b:________
quiz.explanation: a.copy() creates a separate array with its own data, so modifying b will not modify a.

quiz.question: [Copying] Assign array a directly to b so both names refer to the same array object:________
quiz.explanation: A normal assignment does not copy a NumPy array. Both variable names reference the same underlying array object.

quiz.question: [Data Types] Convert array a to integers:________
quiz.explanation: astype() returns a new array converted to the requested data type.

quiz.question: [Data Types] Convert array a to NumPy float32 values:________
quiz.explanation: astype(np.float32) creates a new array whose elements use 32-bit floating-point storage.

quiz.question: [Broadcasting] Add the scalar 10 to every element of array a:________
quiz.explanation: NumPy broadcasts a scalar across every element, so 10 is added element by element without an explicit loop.

quiz.question: [Broadcasting] Add one-dimensional array b to each compatible row of two-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: When the trailing dimensions are compatible, NumPy automatically broadcasts b across a rather than requiring manual repetition.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Perform matrix multiplication of A and B using the @ operator:________
quiz.explanation: The @ operator performs matrix multiplication, unlike *, which performs element-wise multiplication.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Perform matrix multiplication of A and B using a NumPy function:________
quiz.explanation: np.matmul() performs matrix multiplication and is the function counterpart to the @ operator.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Compute the dot product of arrays a and b:________
quiz.explanation: For one-dimensional arrays, np.dot() computes the vector dot product. Its behavior for higher-dimensional arrays differs from simple element-wise multiplication.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Compute the inverse of square matrix A:________
quiz.explanation: np.linalg.inv() returns the matrix inverse when A is square and nonsingular.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Compute the determinant of square matrix A:________
quiz.explanation: np.linalg.det() computes the determinant of a square matrix.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of square matrix A:________
quiz.explanation: np.linalg.eig() returns a tuple containing eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Solve the linear system A x = b for x:________
quiz.explanation: np.linalg.solve() directly solves a square system of linear equations and is generally preferable to explicitly computing the inverse.

quiz.question: [Linear Algebra] Compute the vector or matrix norm of a:________
quiz.explanation: np.linalg.norm() computes a norm; for a 1D vector the default is the Euclidean norm.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Create NumPy's modern random number generator:________
quiz.explanation: default_rng() creates a Generator instance, which is the recommended modern interface for NumPy random-number generation.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Generate 5 random floats in [0, 1) using generator rng:________
quiz.explanation: Generator.random() produces uniformly distributed floating-point values in [0, 1).

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Generate 5 random integers from 0 through 9 using generator rng:________
quiz.explanation: Generator.integers(low, high, size) includes low and excludes high, so this produces values from 0 to 9.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Generate 5 values from a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1:________
quiz.explanation: Generator.normal() samples from a normal distribution with the specified mean and standard deviation.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Randomly choose 5 values from [1, 2, 3] using generator rng:________
quiz.explanation: Generator.choice() randomly samples elements from the supplied sequence.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Shuffle array a in place using generator rng:________
quiz.explanation: Generator.shuffle() randomly reorders the elements of an array in place.

quiz.question: [Random Numbers] Create a reproducible random generator using seed 42:________
quiz.explanation: Passing a fixed seed makes the generated pseudo-random sequence reproducible across runs with the same NumPy behavior.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Represent a missing floating-point value using NaN:________
quiz.explanation: np.nan is NumPy's floating-point NaN value, commonly used to represent missing or undefined numeric data.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Create a Boolean mask showing where array a contains NaN values:________
quiz.explanation: np.isnan() returns True for elements that are NaN and False otherwise.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Remove NaN values from a one-dimensional array a:________
quiz.explanation: np.isnan(a) identifies NaNs, ~ negates the mask, and Boolean indexing keeps only non-NaN values.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Sum array a while ignoring NaN values:________
quiz.explanation: np.nansum() computes the sum while treating NaN values as missing rather than propagating NaN.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Compute the mean of array a while ignoring NaN values:________
quiz.explanation: np.nanmean() calculates the average using only non-NaN values.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Get the minimum value of array a while ignoring NaN values:________
quiz.explanation: np.nanmin() returns the minimum among non-NaN values.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Get the maximum value of array a while ignoring NaN values:________
quiz.explanation: np.nanmax() returns the maximum among non-NaN values.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Create a Boolean mask showing where array a contains positive or negative infinity:________
quiz.explanation: np.isinf() returns True for positive or negative infinity and False for finite values and NaN.

quiz.question: [Missing & Invalid Values] Create a Boolean mask showing where array a contains finite numeric values:________
quiz.explanation: np.isfinite() returns True for values that are neither infinity nor NaN.

quiz.question: [Clipping] Limit every value of array a to the inclusive range from 0 to 50:________
quiz.explanation: np.clip() replaces values below the lower bound with that bound and values above the upper bound with the upper bound.

quiz.question: [Adding & Removing Elements] Append the value 10 to array a and return the new array:________
quiz.explanation: np.append() returns a new array with the added value; it does not resize the original array in place.

quiz.question: [Adding & Removing Elements] Insert the value 100 into array a at index 2 and return the new array:________
quiz.explanation: np.insert() returns a new array with values inserted before the requested index.

quiz.question: [Adding & Removing Elements] Delete the element at index 2 from array a and return the new array:________
quiz.explanation: np.delete() returns a new array with the specified element or elements removed.

quiz.question: [Vectorization] Select values greater than 10 from array a and multiply those selected values by 2 without an explicit Python loop:________
quiz.explanation: This combines Boolean indexing and vectorized multiplication, a common NumPy pattern that avoids writing an explicit Python loop.
